title: One Lord, one faith, one baptism (Ephesians 4:1–6)
hookLine: keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace

lines: A CHURCH OF JEWS AND GENTILES.
cards: Some families have a quarrel that comes back every holiday: the same two people, the same old topic, the same tight silence over dessert.
Churches have them too, and the church Paul writes to in Ephesians was mixed: Jews and Gentiles, people who'd grown up with very different ways.
So he opens the second half of the letter by begging them, as a prisoner in the Lord, to walk worthy of their calling: with humility, gentleness and patience, bearing with one another in love.
And then he tells them what they're keeping.

teach.b: "Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." Notice the verb. Keep, not make.
Paul doesn't tell them to build unity from scratch. He says it's already given, and their job is to guard it.
The word for bond is syndesmos, the same word a verse in Colossians uses for the ligaments that hold a body together. Peace is the ligament.

Then he counts: "One body and one Spirit; as you are called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all."
Body, Spirit, hope, Lord, faith, baptism, God. Seven. It sounds like something sung or recited, and scholars think Paul may be echoing words the churches already used.

teach.h: ONE LORD, ONE FAITH, ONE BAPTISM.
teach.b: Catholics recite a descendant of that list every Sunday in the Creed: one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church, and one baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
And that one baptism matters for how Catholics see other Christians. The Second Vatican Council taught that baptism is a sacramental bond of unity among all who are reborn by it.

When a baptized Protestant Christian becomes Catholic, the Church does not baptize them again, as long as the baptism was with water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. One baptism.
The Church says plainly that full unity is not yet here. But Paul's verb still stands: keep. Something is already shared, and it can be guarded or neglected.

how: Catholics profess "one baptism for the forgiveness of sins" in the Creed at Sunday Mass, and the Church recognizes the baptism of other Christians baptized with water in the name of the Trinity, so it is not repeated.

games.q: your church is mixed and quarrelsome. you're Paul, writing from prison. what do you ask them to do?
o: split into two churches to keep the peace.
keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
let the majority decide every dispute.
games.why: "careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace": one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism.

practice: Think of one quarrel in your life, small or old, and picture the other person, not the argument.

Notice something you still share, a family, a street, a history, maybe a faith, and one small step that would keep the peace instead of winning. If you pray, pray for them by name; if not, simply wish them well, and mean it.

wordCard.voice: One Lord. From Paul's seven ones in Ephesians: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a bond, a binding together; in Colossians 2:19, a body's ligaments (Ephesians 4:3).

carryVoice: Your line: keep the bond of peace. It's already given; it only needs keeping. Until tomorrow.
